stem: A grower repeatedly increases fertilizer strength in response to pale leaves, but root-zone EC continues rising and the symptoms do not improve. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Continue increasing fertilizer concentration because pale foliage is best interpreted as inadequate nutrient supply even when root-zone EC is already rising and the visual symptom has not improved after previous increases
The diagnosis should be reconsidered and pH, root health, moisture, antagonism, and actual nutrient availability evaluated before adding more fertilizer
Interpret the rising root-zone EC as evidence that roots are taking up nutrients efficiently and maintain the stronger feed until leaf color returns to normal
Change the fertilizer concentration again using leaf color as the main guide, without first checking whether irrigation, pH, roots, or nutrient interactions are limiting uptake
rationale: Persistent symptoms despite rising root-zone EC weaken the assumption of simple nutrient shortage. Availability, root function, irrigation, pH, and nutrient interactions should be evaluated before further increases.
